questions.question: With d_model = 512 and 8 equal heads, what is d_head?
options: 8 dimensions per head
128 dimensions per head
512 dimensions per head
64 dimensions per head
questions.explanation: Equal heads divide the model width: d_head = 512 ÷ 8 = 64 dimensions. A 128-dimensional head would use 8 × 128 = 1,024 dimensions, twice the stated model width.

questions.question: What shape does each attention head produce before the heads are concatenated?
options: (N, d_head)
(d_model, n_heads)
(N, N, d_model)
(n_heads, N, d_model)
questions.explanation: Each head attends over N token positions and returns one d_head-wide vector per position, so its output is (N, d_head). The N × N attention matrix contains weights; summing weighted values removes that middle position axis.

questions.question: After head outputs are concatenated, what does the learned W_o projection do?
options: Adds positional embeddings before attention begins
Splits each head into separate key and value streams
Applies a different softmax to every token label
Mixes information across the concatenated heads
questions.explanation: After concatenating head outputs, W_o applies a learned projection across the full d_model width, allowing information from different heads to mix. Positional embeddings enter before attention; W_o is not where they are added.

questions.question: At the same sequence length and per-head width, a model uses 64 query heads and 8 KV heads. By what factor can GQA shrink KV-cache storage versus MHA?
options: 56 times smaller
8 times smaller
16 times smaller
4 times smaller
questions.explanation: KV-cache storage is proportional to the number of stored key/value heads, so the ratio is 64 ÷ 8 = 8×. The value 56 is the difference in head counts, not the storage factor.

questions.question: Inference memory is dominated by stored key/value states. Which attention variant is the direct fit in the lesson?
options: A wider feed-forward layer with more parameters
Multi-head attention with one KV pair per query
Grouped-query attention with fewer KV heads
A larger output projection after concatenation
questions.explanation: GQA shares fewer key/value heads across query heads, directly reducing the states that inference must store. Multi-head attention with one KV pair per query stores a KV pair for every query head, so it does not address cache-dominated memory.

questions.question: A head-splitting implementation receives d_model = 510 and n_heads = 8. What should happen?
options: Reject the configuration because the width does not divide evenly
Pad each head to 64 dimensions without changing the input
Run one attention head with a larger output projection
Treat the remaining six dimensions as an extra head
questions.explanation: Equal-width splitting requires d_model/n_heads to be an integer, but 510 ÷ 8 = 63.75. The implementation asserts divisibility; padding to 64 changes the input width and is not an implicit split operation.
